note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, after 66858fa127). RFC 7606 Section 4: "In either of these cases, an error condition exists and the "treat- as-withdraw" approach MUST be used (unless some other, more severe error is encountered dictating a stronger approach)"; the first case is "the length of the last encountered path attribute would cause the Total Attribute Length to be exceeded when parsing the enclosed path attributes." Changed unit: TestRFC7606AttributeLengthConflictTreatAsWithdraw lost its RFC8654-3-1 tag and gained an RFC 7606 quote and a claim naming exactly what it asserts; body unchanged. Buffer isolates case 1: ORIGIN, AS_PATH, NEXT_HOP, then COMMUNITY declaring 8 (a legal COMMUNITY length, so 7.8 cannot fire) with 4 octets following; hasNLRI=true, so the Section 5.2 escalation in structuralError does not apply. Exact TreatAsWithdraw, AttrCode 8 and "Section 4" text: a reset or a silent accept both fail it. Producer read: ValidateUpdateRFC7606AddPath bounds check returns structuralError (treat-as-withdraw with reachable NLRI); every session-reset check returns immediately, so the collected strongest before a structural exit is never above treat-as-withdraw and the "more severe" carve-out is not downgraded. Case 2 is TestRFC7606FewerThanThreeOctetsRemainTreatAsWithdraw (1 and 2 trailing octets, 3 with Extended Length: exact TreatAsWithdraw; clean mandatory set: exact None). Positives: that clean control and the exact-None baselines of TestRFC7606SystematicLengthCorruption. Verdict stands.
